caption:
What if the strongest case for greening our operations is what clean energy enables beyond carbon?

UNDP’s new Greening Moonshot report offers a useful answer.

Halfway to 2030, we have reduced operational emissions by 25 percent compared with 2018. More than 200 projects now reduce over 4,000 tonnes of CO₂e each year while saving nearly $2 million annually in energy costs. Every $1 invested in green energy solutions now delivers around $8.5 in lifetime energy savings.

But the development story goes further.

⚡ Reliable energy enables delivery. In Afghanistan, more than 370 kWp of solar capacity is reducing dependence on diesel where the national grid is unreliable. In Haiti, renewable energy supplies around two-thirds of office power through chronic blackouts and fuel shortages.

💰 Efficiency creates development resources. Greening investments have enabled more than $21 million to be reprogrammed to country priorities.

📊 Data makes the transition smarter. Different energy systems require different solutions. Solar and batteries make sense for generator-dependent offices. E-mobility can deliver greater gains where electricity is already clean.

This is why I increasingly see clean energy as development infrastructure.

It keeps teams working, reduces exposure to energy shocks and frees resources for the communities we serve.

The energy transition succeeds when it improves how development is delivered.
